root_cause: Two valuation errors in the charge score. (1) _score_charge_target credited ch_damage = full expected melee damage x2, also the part past the target's remaining wounds: at s7480 r3 P2 the Allarus (7.5 dmg) got 15 points of ch_damage against a 2-wound remnant (target_hp 2), the same order as the 7-HP Blade Champion (20). (2) 11e 11.04 targets are picked after the roll and _select_post_roll_charge_targets re-picks the best enemy in reach when the roll misses every declared target, so every declaration's real value is an EV over 2D6 including that fallback. The multi-target combos (_score_multi_target_combo) were scored that way, single-target declarations were scored as value x P(reach) with no fallback, so 'near remnant 3+ + far unit 9+' (EV 42.0) beat 'Blade Champion 5+, remnant on 3-4' (scored 32.9, real EV ~38.9). Together the remnant combo won.
fix_summary: FIX_CHARGE_TARGET (default 1.0, 0 = base exactly). CT-CAP: ch_damage credits min(melee damage, target's remaining wounds). CT-FALLBACK (11e only): new _charge_post_roll_fallback_ev(declared, scored_targets) = sum over rolls below every declared target of P(roll) x value-if-reached (score/prob) of the target the post-roll step would re-pick (highest raw target score in reach); added as term ch_post_roll_fallback to each single-target declaration and to each multi-target combo's EV, so singles and combos compare like for like. Best-pick for the unit is taken after all its targets are scored. Log lines tagged [CHARGE_TARGET] (CT-CAP and fallback).

fires: Replays (fix in both seats, game to end of next round): ch_post_roll_fallback term present on 7/10/2/10/11/2/8 candidates in 5/4/2/5/5/2/6 charge decisions (f1, f2, f3, g1, g2, g3, g4); decisions changed at the measured positions: f1 and f2 only. Bench (mirror_custodes_2000_postdeploy, seed 93101, fix in candidate seat only): 55 and 153 [CHARGE_TARGET] lines in the two games (CT-CAP 22/53, fallback 33/100). These lines log score changes, not only changed decisions (CT-CAP also fires from the post-roll re-pick); the number of changed declarations per game was not counted. Pair margin -1.5 (1 pair, no signal).
risks: (1) It re-ranks charge targets in most charge phases (frequent fires): broad effect, measured only at 1 clear finding + 4 guardrails; needs the full-game bench. (2) CT-FALLBACK lifts the score of far first-choice declarations (e.g. +62 on a 10+ target whose fallback is a near unit), which can change WHICH unit charges first (best_score across units, _build_charge_order) even when each unit's target set is similar; the charge threshold (~0.37) almost never binds so charge/no-charge is mostly unchanged, so it doesn't fix the 'should not charge' sub-findings (s7465 r2 P1 still charges). (3) In f1 the fix's own choice is A#2-first (objective x1.5) rather than Blade Champion-first; 12-seed check +4.58 but CI crosses 0. (4) CT-CAP stops paying for overkill, so a unit may now prefer a fresh big target over finishing a remnant on an objective; ch_can_wipe and objective multipliers still reward the finish, but over 5 rounds a missed 'clear the objective' kill (primary + secondaries like Assassination/Bring It Down) could cost VP. (5) Fallback model uses the AI's scored DECLARE_CHARGE targets (>=3% chance) as the selectable pool; the real pool is every enemy within 12" and the roll, so it can slightly under-count.
